questions.q: Which one of the following series contains only electrophiles?
questions.solution:
Electrophiles are electron-deficient species that can accept an electron pair. They are either positively charged or neutral molecules with an incomplete octet or highly polar bonds.

In the first series, $\text{R-OH}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ have lone pairs on oxygen and nitrogen respectively, making them nucleophiles.

In the second series, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{R}_2\text{N}^-$ have lone pairs and a negative charge respectively, making them nucleophiles.

In the third series, $\text{BF}_3$ is an electron-deficient Lewis acid with an incomplete octet. $\text{SO}_3$ has a highly electron-deficient sulfur atom due to three electronegative oxygen atoms. $\text{NO}^+$ is a positively charged ion. All three are electrophiles.

In the fourth series, $\text{R-NH}_2$ has a lone pair on nitrogen, making it a nucleophile.

Answer: $\text{BF}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{NO}^+$

Let us examine each carbon atom in the principal chain for chirality by checking if it is bonded to four different groups:

$C_1$: Bonded to three identical hydrogen atoms, hence achiral.

$C_2$: Bonded to $-H$, $-I$, $-CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different, making $C_2$ a chiral center.

$C_3$: Bonded to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(I)CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different, making $C_3$ a chiral center.

$C_4$: Bonded to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(CH_3)_2$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(I)CH_3$. All four groups are different, making $C_4$ a chiral center.

$C_5$: Bonded to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH_3$ (from $C_6$), and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(I)CH_3$. Since it is bonded to two identical methyl groups, $C_5$ is achiral.

$C_6$: Bonded to three identical hydrogen atoms, hence achiral.

The methyl substituents on $C_3$, $C_4$, and $C_5$ are also bonded to three identical hydrogen atoms and are achiral.

Thus, there are exactly $3$ chiral carbon atoms (C_2$, $C_3$, and $C_4$).

Answer: 3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the name of second lower homologue of $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{COOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The given compound is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{COOH}$, which contains 4 carbon atoms and is named butanoic acid.

Homologues in a series differ by a successive $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit.

The first lower homologue has one less $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (propanoic acid).

The second lower homologue has two less $-\text{CH}_2-$ units, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ (ethanoic acid).

Answer: Ethanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following elements is NOT present in mustard gas?
questions.solution:
The chemical name of mustard gas is bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide.

Its chemical structure is $\text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{S}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ and its molecular formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{Cl}_2\text{S}$.

The elements present in mustard gas are Carbon ($\text{C}$), Hydrogen ($\text{H}$), Chlorine ($\text{Cl}$), and Sulphur ($\text{S}$).

Nitrogen ($\text{N}$) is not present in mustard gas.

Answer: $\text{N}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
The given compound contains a seven-membered carbon ring with a principal functional group, an alcohol (-OH). Thus, the parent name is cycloheptanol.

The carbon atom attached to the -OH group is numbered as C1.

The substituents on the ring are an ethyl group and a methyl group.

Numbering the ring to assign the lowest possible locants to the substituents yields two possibilities: clockwise gives positions 3 for ethyl and 6 for methyl, while counter-clockwise gives positions 3 for methyl and 6 for ethyl.

When the set of locants is the same in both directions, alphabetical order is considered. Since 'ethyl' comes before 'methyl' alphabetically, the ethyl group is assigned the lower number (3).

Therefore, the correct numbering places the ethyl group at C3 and the methyl group at C6.

The complete IUPAC name is 3-Ethyl-6-methylcycloheptanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements is NOT true about homologous series?
options: Each member of a series has same functional group.
Each member has same type of carbon skeleton.
Each member differs by ethylene group from next member.
All members of series possess similar chemical properties.
questions.solution:
A homologous series is a series of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, and the same general formula.

Successive members of a homologous series differ from each other by a methylene group ($-CH_2-$) and a molecular mass of $14\text{ u}$.

The statement that each member differs by an ethylene group is incorrect, as they differ by a methylene group.

Answer: Each member differs by ethylene group from next member.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is haloalkyne?
questions.solution:
A haloalkyne (or alkynyl halide) is a compound in which a halogen atom is directly bonded to an $sp$-hybridized carbon atom of the carbon-carbon triple bond.

In chloroethyne (Cl-C \equiv CH$), the chlorine atom is directly attached to the $sp$-hybridized carbon atom. Therefore, it is a haloalkyne.

In 3-chloropropyne (HC \equiv C-CH_2-Cl$), 1-chloropent-2-yne (CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv C-CH_2-Cl$), and 4-chloropent-2-yne (CH_3-CH(Cl)-C \equiv C-CH_3$), the chlorine atom is attached to an $sp^3$-hybridized carbon atom.

Answer: Chloroethyne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following has the highest nucleophilicity ?
questions.solution:
The given species $\text{CH}_3^-$, $\text{NH}_2^-$, $\text{OH}^-$, and $\text{F}^-$ have donor atoms belonging to the same period (Period 2) of the periodic table.

Across a period from left to right, the electronegativity of the atoms increases in the order $\text{C} < \text{N} < \text{O} < \text{F}$.

A more electronegative atom holds its lone pair of electrons more tightly, making it less available for donation to an electrophile. Therefore, nucleophilicity decreases as electronegativity increases.

The order of nucleophilicity is $\text{CH}_3^- > \text{NH}_2^- > \text{OH}^- > \text{F}^-$.

Thus, $\text{CH}_3^-$ has the highest nucleophilicity.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the number of hyperconjugation structures in the isopropyl carbocation.
questions.solution:
The structure of the isopropyl carbocation is $(CH_3)_2CH^+$.

The carbon atom bearing the positive charge is attached to two methyl groups.

The number of $\alpha$-hydrogens is the total number of hydrogen atoms attached to the $\alpha$-carbons.

Here, there are two $\alpha$-carbons, each having $3$ hydrogen atoms. Thus, the total number of $\alpha$-hydrogens is $3 + 3 = 6$.

The number of hyperconjugation structures is equal to the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Therefore, the number of hyperconjugation structures is $6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of following reactions, the oxidative rancidity is?
questions.solution:
Oxidative rancidity is the process of autoxidation of lipids (fats and oils) exposed to oxygen, resulting in unpleasant odors and flavors.

This autoxidation proceeds via a free radical chain reaction mechanism.

The mechanism involves three main steps: initiation (formation of lipid free radicals), propagation (reaction of lipid radicals with oxygen to form peroxyl radicals, which abstract hydrogen from other lipid molecules), and termination (combination of radicals to form stable, non-radical products).

Therefore, oxidative rancidity is a free radical chain reaction.

Answer: free radical chain reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an aromatic alcohol?
questions.solution:
Aromatic alcohols are compounds in which the hydroxyl ($-OH$) group is attached to a carbon atom of an aliphatic side chain, rather than directly to the aromatic ring.

If the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the aromatic ring, the compound is classified as a phenol.

In compounds (I) and (IV), the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the benzene ring. Hence, they are phenols.

In compounds (II) and (III), the $-OH$ group is attached to a $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom of the side chain. Hence, they are aromatic alcohols.

Answer: II and III Only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
(A). Inductive effect(I). Delocalization of $\pi$ electrons
(B). Hyper-conjugation(II). Displacement of $\pi$ electrons
(C). Resonance effect(III). Delocalization of $\sigma$ electrons
(IV). Displacement of $\sigma$ electrons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Inductive effect involves the permanent displacement of $\sigma$ electrons along a saturated carbon chain due to differences in electronegativity. Thus, (A) matches with (IV).

Hyper-conjugation involves the delocalization of $\sigma$ electrons (typically from a C-H bond) into an adjacent empty p-orbital or $\pi$ system. Thus, (B) matches with (III).

Resonance effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$ electrons or lone pairs across a conjugated system. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

The correct matching is (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I).

Answer: $(A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the compound $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH=CHCOOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid ($-\text{COOH}$), so numbering starts from the carbon atom of the $-\text{COOH}$ group.

The longest carbon chain containing the principal functional group has $6$ carbon atoms, so the root word is 'hex'.

There are two double bonds located at C2 and C4, so the primary suffix is '2,4-diene'.

The secondary suffix for the carboxylic acid is 'oic acid'.

Combining these parts, the IUPAC name of the compound is Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid.

Answer: Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for a molecule that has two amino groups in opposing (para) locations around a benzene ring?
questions.solution:
The molecule consists of a benzene ring with two amino ($-NH_2$) groups attached at opposite positions.

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the parent hydrocarbon is benzene.

The two amino groups are indicated by the suffix "diamine".

The positions of the amino groups are numbered to give them the lowest possible locants. Since they are at opposite positions (para), the locants are $1$ and $4$.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is benzene-1,4-diamine.

Answer: Benzene-1,4-diamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following, the most stable carbocation is
questions.solution:
The stability of carbocations increases with the increase in the number of alkyl groups attached to the positively charged carbon atom. This is due to the +I (inductive) effect and hyperconjugation.

The order of stability of alkyl carbocations is $3^{{}^{\circ}} > 2^{{}^{\circ}} > 1^{{}^{\circ}} > \text{methyl}$.

Among the given options, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$ is a tertiary (3^{{}^{\circ}}$) carbocation, which has nine \alpha$-hydrogen atoms, leading to maximum hyperconjugation structures. Hence, it is the most stable carbocation.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following is correct decreasing order of acidic strength for the compounds listed below?
I: p-chlorophenol, II: p-Cresol, III: p-nitrophenol, IV: p-methoxyphenol.
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of phenols is directly proportional to the stability of the phenoxide ion formed after losing a proton.

Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize the phenoxide ion through $-I$ and $-R$ effects, thereby increasing the acidic strength. Electron-donating groups destabilize the phenoxide ion through $+I$, $+H$, and $+R$ effects, thereby decreasing the acidic strength.

In p-nitrophenol (III), the $-NO_2$ group exerts strong $-R$ and $-I$ effects, making it the most acidic.

In p-chlorophenol (I), the $-Cl$ group exerts a $-I$ effect which dominates over its $+R$ effect, making it more acidic than phenol but less acidic than p-nitrophenol.

In p-cresol (II), the $-CH_3$ group exerts $+I$ and hyperconjugation ($+H$) effects, decreasing the acidic strength compared to phenol.

In p-methoxyphenol (IV), the $-OCH_3$ group exerts a strong $+R$ effect which dominates over its $-I$ effect, making it the least acidic.

Thus, the decreasing order of acidic strength is III > I > II > IV.

Answer: III > I > II > IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital formed by overlap of p-orbitals must contain,
questions.solution:
According to H\u00fcckel's rule, a cyclic, planar, and completely conjugated system is highly stable and aromatic if it contains $(4n + 2)\pi$-electrons, where $n$ is an integer (0, 1, 2, \dots$).

These \pi$-electrons reside in the cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital formed by the continuous lateral overlap of unhybridized p-orbitals of the atoms in the ring.

Thus, the cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital must contain $(4n + 2)$ p electrons for the system to exhibit aromatic stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are TRUE?
(I) Inductive effect operates through the sigma bond
(II) Resonance effect operates through the pi bond
(III) Inductive effects operate through the pi bond
(IV) Resonance effect operates through the sigma bond
questions.solution:
Inductive effect involves the displacement of $\sigma$-electrons along a saturated carbon chain. Thus, it operates through $\sigma$-bonds.

Resonance effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs of electrons. Thus, it operates through $\pi$-bonds.

Therefore, statements (I) and (II) are true.

Answer: (I) and (II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the false statement regarding chirality from the following.
options: $SN^1$ reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
A recemic mixture shows zero dipole rotation
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other
The product obtained by $SN^2$ reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
questions.solution:
Enantiomers are defined as stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. Therefore, the statement that enantiomers are superimposable mirror images is false.

In an $S_N1$ reaction, the formation of a planar carbocation intermediate allows the nucleophile to attack from either face with equal probability, generally yielding a 1:1 mixture of enantiomers (a racemic mixture).

A racemic mixture contains equal amounts of dextrorotatory and levorotatory enantiomers, resulting in zero net optical rotation.

In an $S_N2$ reaction at a chiral center, the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group, leading to a complete inversion of configuration.

Answer: Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the difference in terms of molar masses of second and fourth members of homologous series?
questions.solution:
Successive members of a homologous series differ by a $-CH_2-$ group.

The molar mass of a $-CH_2-$ group is $12 + 2 \times 1 = 14 \text{ g/mol}$.

The difference between the second and fourth members of a homologous series corresponds to two $-CH_2-$ groups.

Difference in molar mass $= 2 \times 14 = 28 \text{ g/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of isomerism is exhibited by neopentane?
questions.solution:
Neopentane (C_5H_{12}$) is an isomer of pentane.

The isomers of pentane are n-pentane, isopentane, and neopentane.

These compounds have the same molecular formula but differ in the arrangement of their carbon skeleton (straight chain versus branched chain).

Therefore, neopentane exhibits chain isomerism.

Answer: chain$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of ' C ' and ' H ' atoms respectively present in n mole molecule represented by following structure ?
questions.solution:
The molecular structure of styrene consists of a benzene ring bonded to a vinyl group.

A benzene ring attached as a substituent contributes 6 carbon atoms and 5 hydrogen atoms, while the vinyl group $\mathrm{-CH=CH_2}$ contributes 2 carbon atoms and 3 hydrogen atoms.

Total carbon atoms: $6 + 2 = 8$

Total hydrogen atoms: $5 + 3 = 8$

The molecular formula is $\mathrm{C8H8}$.

For $n$ moles of styrene molecules, the number of moles of carbon atoms is $8 \times n = 8n$, and the number of moles of hydrogen atoms is $8 \times n = 8n$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is trihydric phenol?
questions.solution:
Phenols are classified by the number of hydroxyl groups bonded to the benzene ring: monohydric (one $\mathrm{-OH}$), dihydric (two $\mathrm{-OH}$), or trihydric (three $\mathrm{-OH}$).

Catechol (benzene-1,2-diol), resorcinol (benzene-1,3-diol), and quinol (benzene-1,4-diol) are all dihydric phenols.

Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol and contains three hydroxyl groups.

Thus, pyrogallol is the only trihydric phenol among the options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the difference of molar masses expressed in gram of two neighbouring members of a homologous series?
questions.solution:
A homologous series consists of compounds with the same functional group, where each successive member differs by a $\text{CH}_2$ group.

The molar mass of $\text{CH}_2$ is calculated as $12 \text{ g/mol} + 2 \times 1 \text{ g/mol} = 14 \text{ g/mol}$.

The difference in molar masses is 14 g/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to carbinol system tert butyl alcohol is named as,
questions.solution:
In the carbinol system, alcohols are named as derivatives of methanol by replacing hydrogen atoms on the methyl group with substituents.

Tert-butyl alcohol has the formula $(CH_3)_3C\text{--}OH$, where the carbinol carbon is bonded to three methyl groups. This corresponds to trimethyl carbinol.

The alternatives correspond to different structures: methyl carbinol (CH_3CH_2OH$), ethyl carbinol (CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$), and propyl carbinol (CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2OH$).

The correct carbinol system name is therefore trimethyl carbinol.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Select from the following a correct IUPAC name of pyrogallol.
questions.solution:
Pyrogallol is the common name for 1,2,3-trihydroxybenzene. In IUPAC nomenclature, the parent structure is benzene, with hydroxyl groups located at positions 1, 2, and 3.

Evaluating the options: A corresponds to resorcinol, B to hydroquinone, C correctly identifies pyrogallol as benzene-1,2,3-triol, and D corresponds to phloroglucinol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The common name of Benzene - 1,2 - diol is
questions.solution:
Benzene-1,2-diol features two hydroxyl groups at adjacent positions on the aromatic ring, corresponding to the common name catechol.

For comparison, benzene-1,3-diol is known as resorcinol, benzene-1,4-diol is quinol (or hydroquinone), and benzene-1,2,3-triol is pyrogallol.

The correct answer is A. Catechol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common name of Benzene-1,3-diol?
questions.solution:
The common name for Benzene-1,3-diol is resorcinol, corresponding to isomer position 1,3.

Benzene-1,2-diol is catechol, while benzene-1,4-diol is hydroquinone or quinol. Pyrogallol is the trihydroxybenzene 1,2,3-isomer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the difference in molar mass of Undecane and Dodecane?
questions.solution:
Alkanes follow the general formula $C_nH_{2n+2}$.
For undecane (n=11$): $C_{11}H_{24}$
For dodecane (n=12$): $C_{12}H_{26}$

Using atomic masses $C \approx 12.01 \text{ g/mol}$ and $H \approx 1.008 \text{ g/mol}$:
Undecane molar mass: $11 \times 12.01 + 24 \times 1.008 = 156.302 \text{ g/mol}$
Dodecane molar mass: $12 \times 12.01 + 26 \times 1.008 = 170.328 \text{ g/mol}$

The difference is $170.328 - 156.302 = 14.026 \text{ g/mol}$, which rounds to $14 \text{ g/mol}$.

Equivalently, consecutive alkanes differ by a $CH_2$ group with molar mass $12.01 + 2 \times 1.008 = 14.026 \text{ g/mol}$.

Correct option: D $14 \text{ g/mol}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds does NOT contain nitrogen in it?
questions.solution:
Thiophene has the formula $C_4H_4S$ and contains sulfur but no nitrogen. All other options contain nitrogen: pyridine (C_5H_5N$), pyrrole (C_4H_5N$), and piperidine (C_5H_{11}N$) are nitrogenous heterocycles.

The compound that does not contain nitrogen is thiophene.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is an optically inactive compound?
questions.solution:
Optical inactivity arises in achiral molecules. A compound lacking chiral centers or possessing a plane of symmetry is achiral and thus optically inactive.

For 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, the carbon at position 2 is bonded to $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with two identical methyl groups making it non-chiral. No other chiral centers exist, and the molecule lacks a plane of symmetry, confirming achirality.

In contrast, 3-chlorohexane has one chiral center at $C3$ with groups $- \text{H}$, $- \text{Cl}$, $- \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $- \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, all distinct. 2-chloropentane and 2-chloro-3-methylbutane each possess a chiral center at $C2$, bonded to distinct groups, ensuring chirality and optical activity.

Only 2-chloro-2-methylbutane is achiral and optically inactive.

questions.explanation:

Only 2-chloro-2-methylbutane is achiral and optically inactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
Identifying the IUPAC name requires analyzing the structure: a cyclobutane ring with substituents including a methoxy group and two methyl groups.

Numbering begins at the carbon bearing the methoxy group to maintain the lowest possible locants. The adjacent carbon, with two methyl groups, is assigned position 2.

The correct name is $\text{1-methoxy-2,2-dimethylcyclobutane}$, matching option C. Option A and B incorrectly identify the parent as butane rather than cyclobutane, and option D uses non-optimal numbering for the methoxy group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds does NOT contain oxygen as heteroatom?
questions.solution:
Identification of compounds without oxygen heteroatoms: Among the given options, pyrrole contains nitrogen as the sole heteroatom and lacks oxygen entirely.

Furan features an oxygen heteroatom in its five-membered aromatic ring structure $C_4H_4O$.

Tetrahydrofuran contains oxygen in its saturated five-membered ring $C_4H_8O$.

4H-Pyran incorporates oxygen in its six-membered ring structure $C_5H_6O$.

Pyrrole $C_4H_5N$ contains nitrogen as its heteroatom without oxygen participation.

Since pyrrole is the only compound devoid of oxygen, the correct choice is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many chiral carbon atoms are present in 2-chloro-3,4,5-trimethylhexane?
questions.solution:
Identifying chiral carbon atoms in 2-chloro-3,4,5-trimethylhexane

The compound has structure: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Cl)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3}$

Chiral centers require carbon bonded to four distinct groups. Terminal methyl carbons (C1 and C6) have three identical hydrogens and are not chiral.

Carbons C2, C3, C4, and C5 each have four different substituents:
C2: H, Cl, CH_3, and $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH_3}$
C3: H, CH_3, $\mathrm{-CH(Cl)CH_3}$, and $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH_3}$
C4: H, CH_3, $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(Cl)CH_3}$, and $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH_3}$
C5: H, $CH_3$, $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(Cl)CH_3}$, and $CH_3$

All four internal carbons satisfy the chirality condition.

Final answer: $\boxed{4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is structural formula of mesityl oxide?
questions.solution:
The compound mesityl oxide is systematically named 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one, indicating a five-carbon chain with a ketone at position 2, a double bond at position 3, and a methyl substituent at position 4.

The correct structural formula must correspond to $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH=C(CH_3)-CH_3}$, which is 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one under standard numbering.

Option A, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CH-CH=CH-CO-CH_3}$, is 5-methylhex-3-en-2-one.
Option B, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{C=CH-CO-CH_3}$, expands to $\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CO-CH_3}$ and corresponds to 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.
Option C, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C-CH=CH-CO-CH_3}$, is 5,5-dimethylhex-3-en-2-one.
Option D, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CH-CH=CH-CO-CH(CH_3)_2}$, is 2,6-dimethylhept-3-en-4-one.

Only option B matches the structure of mesityl oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is a pair of functional isomers?
questions.solution:
Functional isomers are compounds sharing the same molecular formula but differing in their functional groups. Option B satisfies this criterion as the two compounds are both $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ but contain alcohol and ether groups respectively.

Butan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) is an alcohol, while 1-methoxypropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is an ether.

The remaining options involve pairs that are isomers but share the same functional group, such as alcohols (A) or ethers (C and D), making them positional or chain isomers rather than functional isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkenes does NOT exhibit cis-trans isomerism ?
questions.solution:
Cis-trans isomerism requires that each carbon of the double bond be bonded to two distinct groups. But-1-ene, with structure $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$, has both hydrogens attached to the first carbon and thus fails this condition.
But-2-ene, 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene, and pent-2-ene all meet the requirement with different substituents on each olefinic carbon, so only but-1-ene lacks geometric isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a non benzenoid aromatic compound?
questions.solution:
Non-benzenoid aromatic compounds satisfy Hückel's rule while lacking a benzene ring structure.

Aniline contains a benzene ring, making it benzenoid aromatic.

Naphthalene consists of fused benzene rings, classifying it as benzenoid aromatic.

Phenol features a benzene ring substituent, rendering it benzenoid aromatic.

Tropone forms a seven-membered cycloheptatrienone ring with $6\pi$ electrons satisfying Hückel's rule (4n + 2$ where $n = 1$), establishing it as non-benzenoid aromatic.

The non-benzenoid aromatic compound is therefore \boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the following compound?
questions.solution:
IUPAC nomenclature follows priority rules where aldehyde and carboxylic acid groups both take precedence, but benzaldehyde derivatives permit common naming conventions.

The compound contains aldehyde, carboxylic acid, and methyl substituents on a benzene ring. While carboxylic acid holds higher priority, benzaldehyde serves as an acceptable parent name when it yields clearer nomenclature. Numbering begins at the aldehyde carbon (C-1), placing carboxylic acid ortho at C-2 and methyl para at C-4.

Substituents are listed alphabetically: carboxy precedes methyl. The systematic name becomes 2-carboxy-4-methylbenzaldehyde.

Among the options, this corresponds to choice A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of structural isomers possible for alkene with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{10}$ ?
questions.solution:
The degree of unsaturation for $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{10}$ is determined by the formula $\text{DU} = x + 1 - \frac{y}{2}$ where $x = 5$ and $y = 10$. Substituting gives $\text{DU} = 5 + 1 - \frac{10}{2} = 1$, indicating one double bond.

Structural isomers with one carbon-carbon double bond and molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{10}$ are enumerated based on chain length and branching. The straight-chain isomers include pent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$, and pent-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$.

Branched-chain isomers are derived from butene with methyl substitution: 2-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$
3-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_3$
and 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$

This totals five structural isomers with no cyclic structures considered.

Final Answer: $\boxed{5}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is primary allylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
A primary allylic alcohol requires that the hydroxyl group is attached to a carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (allylic) and that the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is only attached to one other carbon (primary).

Option A: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option C: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-C(CH_3)_2 -OH}$ is allylic and tertiary.

Option D: $\mathrm{CH_3 -CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option B: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH_2 -OH}$ is allylic since the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group is adjacent to the double bond, and primary as the hydroxyl-bearing carbon attaches to only one other carbon.

The correct primary allylic alcohol is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is vinylic halide?
questions.solution:
Definition of Vinylic Halide: An organic compound where a halogen atom (X$) is bonded directly to an sp^2$ hybridized carbon that is part of a carbon–carbon double bond (C=C$).

A) Haloalkane: The halogen is bonded to an sp^3$ hybridized carbon, as in chloroethane (CH_3CH_2Cl$), which does not satisfy the definition.

B) Haloalkene: Includes structures where the halogen is attached to a carbon in an alkene. Vinylic halides (e.g., chloroethene, $CH_2=CH-Cl$) are a subset, with the halogen on an sp^2$ carbon of the double bond.

C) Haloalkyne: The halogen is bonded to an sp hybridized carbon in a triple bond, such as chloroethyne (CH\equiv C-Cl$), not meeting the criteria.

D) Haloarene: The halogen is on an sp^2$ carbon in an aromatic ring (e.g., chlorobenzene, $C_6H_5Cl$), but “vinylic” specifically denotes non-aromatic alkenes.

Thus, vinylic halides are a type of haloalkene, making B the correct classification.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

Among the given, $\mathrm{BH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$, being electron deficient, behave like electrophiles while $\ddot{\mathrm{N}} \mathrm{H}_{3}$, due to the presence of a lone pair over $\mathrm{N}$, is a nucleophile.
